en: The Sūtra of the Dhāraṇī of the Sublime Gate for Prolonging Life, Spoken by the Buddha.
Translated by the Tripitaka Master of the Western Heaven, the Court Scattered Grandee, Acting Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments,
Great Master of Enlightened Teaching, Dharma-bhadra, by Imperial Decree.
Thus have I heard.

At one time the Buddha was at the Great Enlightenment Site in the kingdom of Magadha, at the place of the Great Miraculous Stupa of the Diamond Throne, in the Hall of Universal Radiance, within the Great Bodhi Mandala.
He was accompanied by a great assembly of one thousand two hundred and fifty śrāvakas,
among whom were the Venerable Śāriputra and the Venerable Mahāmaudgalyāyana.
The Venerable Mahākātyāyana,
the Venerable Mahākāśyapa,
and the Venerable Ānanda.
Venerable Rāhula, Venerable Rakṣita, and Venerable Revata.
The Venerable Cūḷapanthaka, the Venerable Gavāmpati,
and the Venerable Bakkula.
The Venerable Kālodāyin, the Venerable Aniruddha,
and other such venerable ones were all great Arhats.
Furthermore, there was an immeasurable and boundless assembly of great bodhisattvas.
Their names were as follows:
the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajradhvaja.
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Vajragarbha, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi,
and the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Vajrapada.
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Maitreya and such other Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas are all members of the assembly of great Bodhisattvas within this Bhadrakalpa.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi rose from his seat amidst the great assembly,
approached the World-Honored One, joined his palms, and prostrated with his head at the Buddha's feet.
He addressed the Buddha, saying: "I pray only that the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha,
for the sake of benefiting and bringing peace and happiness to all sentient beings,
will proclaim the sublime Dharma of the Dhāraṇī of the Wondrous Door for Extending Life."
This true dharma of the dhāraṇī shall serve as a light that illuminates both me and all sentient beings.
Furthermore, they shall provide protection and rescue,
warding off all those evil Māras who seek an opportunity for harm, as well as all other evils—
namely, those with malicious intent and those with wrathful minds.
Those with extremely evil minds, those with sinful karmic minds,
those with minds of suffering and affliction, and those without a mind of loving-kindness—
including even devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, and mahoragas.
Rākṣasas, bhūtas, piśācas, pretas, kumbhāṇḍas, humans, and non-humans—
all such beings with evil minds will be unable to cause them harm.
Furthermore, neither weapons, poisons, nor any diseases shall be able to cause harm.
Moreover, whether walking, standing, sitting, or lying down, or whether speaking or remaining silent,
one shall be protected, guarded, and kept secure in all places.
We pray that you will proclaim for us the dharani of the sublime gateway to prolonging life.
Why is this? Because this dharani possesses great majestic power;
by relying upon this power, we [shall remain] before the Tathagata.
I shall always deeply respect, serve, and make offerings [to them],
and protect all sentient beings.
World-Honored One, I now act for the great benefit of all sentient beings.
Therefore, we entreat the World-Honored One:
if there are sons or daughters of good family who seek the Bodhisattva vehicle and obtain this dhāraṇī,
they should receive and uphold it with a sincere heart.
Such a person shall receive the protection of the Tathāgata;
even if they are amidst battle arrays, strife, or disease,
or face untimely death, none of such calamities shall be able to harm them.
At that time, the World-Honored One, having accepted the request of the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, praised him, saying: "Excellent, excellent, Vajrapāṇi!
Most excellent, most excellent, Vajrapāṇi!"
Out of your sincere aspiration to benefit all sentient beings, you have made this request.
Listen attentively now, for I shall explain for you the sublime Dharma of the *dhāraṇī* of the wondrous gateway to prolonging life.
Vajrapāṇi, if there are sons or daughters of good family who wish to uphold,
read, and recite the True Dharma of the *Dhāraṇī of the Sublime Gate for Extending Life*,
they must first recite the *Tathāgata-abhiṣeka Dhāraṇī*.
Then he spoke the consecration dhāraṇī, saying:

*ru-ku mu-ku* (1) *ru-gara-maṇi* (2) *pūrṇa-ni samari-cama-ni* (3) *ma-hu ma-hu-ri-ka svāhā* (5). At that time, the World-Honored One, having proclaimed the Tathāgata Consecration Dhāraṇī, [remained silent].
He addressed the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi, saying:
"This Tathāgata-consecration dhāraṇī is able to purify the physical vessel of sentient beings."
Thereafter, one should recite the Dharani of the Sublime Door for Extending Life.
One will then attain the accomplishment of merit free from obstacles and difficulties.
The Dharani of the Sublime Door for Extending Life is now proclaimed as follows:

7. At that time, having spoken this Dharani of the Sublime Door for Prolonging Life, the World-Honored One addressed the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, saying:
"This Dharani of the Sublime Door for Prolonging Life..."
This is indeed that which was taught by the Buddhas of the past, the Truly and Fully Enlightened Ones,
for the sake of benefiting all sentient beings;
one should always receive and uphold it, and proclaim it for others.
These past Buddhas mutually rejoiced in one another and made sincere vows;
I, likewise, for the sake of benefiting all sentient beings,
shall proclaim this dharma of the dhāraṇī.
At that time, having spoken these words,
the World-Honored One immediately emitted from between his eyebrows a ray of light from the mark of a great man,
which universally illuminated all Buddha-fields throughout the ten directions.
And that buddha-field was entirely of one uniform light.
Wherever that light shone, the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, each departed from their own lands and,
in a mere moment, all arrived here in this Sahā world.
They gathered like clouds at the place where the Tathāgata preached the Dharma.
All the Buddhas of the ten directions praised him, saying:
"Excellent, excellent, World-Honored One Śākyamuni Buddha!"
For the sake of benefiting all sentient beings,
he proclaimed this sublime Dharma of the dhāraṇī, the wondrous gateway for extending life,
acting as a brilliant illumination for all beings.
It causes them to rejoice so that they may remember [this teaching],
and it is also able to eradicate all demonic adversaries.
This dhāraṇī, as spoken by the Buddha, I too uphold.
Furthermore, if there are sons or daughters of good family who,
having aroused a heart of utmost sincerity, are constantly able to receive and uphold this dhāraṇī,
and recite it according to the ritual at the time of early dawn;
Such a person shall obtain twenty kinds of merit.
If there is anyone who loves this medicinal herb of such merit,
they should diligently apply themselves with vigor and recite it according to the Dharma.
The aforementioned merits will certainly be obtained.
What are the twenty kinds of merits?
First, one shall uphold all Buddhas.
Second, to serve and make offerings to all Buddhas;
third, to completely extinguish all karmic offenses;
and fourth, to deeply understand the wondrous Dharma.
Fifth, one attains long life; sixth, one’s fame becomes universally renowned; seventh, one attains great wealth and honor;
eighth, one attains great power and influence;
ninth, one constantly remains free from illness.
Tenth, they possess great diligence;
eleventh, they are held in high esteem by the devas;
twelfth, they are cherished by all Buddhas.
Thirteenth, one attains virtuous conduct.
Fourteenth, one attains virtuous benefit.
Fifteenth, one shall become a source of illumination.
Sixteenth, causing them to attain joy;
seventeenth, causing them to attain mindfulness;
eighteenth, possessing the primary and secondary marks upon the body.
Nineteenth, they attain fearlessness.
Twentieth, they are fully endowed with all roots of goodness.
Furthermore, the Buddha addressed the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi:
It is said: "This is the dhāraṇī chapter of the supreme secret dharma of all Tathāgatas, the Perfectly Awakened Ones.
Because it is this dhāraṇī, I proclaim it."
It effectively eliminates all demonic adversaries and is upheld by all Buddhas.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi gave rise to a heart of utmost sincerity.
Joining his palms toward the Buddha, he addressed the World-Honored One, saying:
"World-Honored One, now, relying upon the Buddha's spiritual power,
I wish to act as a protector and benefactor for all sentient beings."
I also rejoice in and proclaim these dhāraṇī verses, the sublime gateway for prolonging life.
World-Honored One, if there should be anyone who receives and maintains them with a sincere heart,
and recites them according to the Dharma at the time of dawn;
Such a person will always receive protection;
even the various māras who seek for an opportunity to strike shall be unable to invade them.
In all places, they will always attain peace and happiness.
Then he spoke the dhāraṇī, saying:
Tadyathā: (1) śikṣi śikṣi, (2) riciri riciri, (3) caca caca caca caca, (4) bibhi bibhi bibhi bibhi, (5) paba paba paba paba, (6) ruru ruru ruru, (7) rara rara rara.

At that time, the Blessed One praised the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi, saying:
Excellent, excellent, Vajrapāṇi!
This most supreme accomplishment of the dhāraṇī of the wondrous gate for prolonging life shall be [taught] for the sake of benefiting and bringing peace and happiness to all sentient beings.
I, too, uphold it. Furthermore,

if there should be anyone who, at the time of early dawn, recites and rejoices in this True Dharma of the Dharani of the Sublime Gate for Prolonging Life according to the ritual rules, [they shall obtain great merit].
Such a person will always receive protection and have their lifespan increased.
At that time, in the assembly, there was Mahābrahmā, the Lord of the Sahā World, who joined his palms toward the Buddha and addressed the Buddha, saying: "World-Honored One," [he said].
I, too, relying on the Buddha’s spiritual power,
shall joyfully proclaim this True Dharma of the Dharani of the Wondrous Gate for Extending Life.
Furthermore, if there is anyone who, at the time of early morning, [recites it]...
To those who, in accordance with the Dharma, recite, uphold,
and maintain this, I shall at all times and in all places provide protection for these sons and daughters of good family, ensuring they attain peace and security.
Then he spoke the dhāraṇī, saying:

Tadyathā | 1. hiri miri ciri svāhā | 2. prahamaśari svāhā | 3. prahama-ni svāhā | 4. supāgi svāhā | 5. puṣpasandhāri svāhā | 6. Blessed One, if there be any son of good family or daughter of good family...
For those who uphold this dhāraṇī,
all evil Māras and various spirits and ghosts who seek an opportunity to harm them shall find no such opportunity.
One should always provide protection in all places.
World-Honored One, for the sake of benefiting and bringing peace and happiness to all sentient beings,
I shall now further recite this dhāraṇī, saying:

*Tadyathā:* 1. *Cilavaraṇi*, 2. *Nāmalani*, 3. *Rici rici*, 4. *Aurī khaṇḍali*, 5. *Sari mahānavaṃtaruṇi*, 6. *Jvalāmarini*, 7. *Cakravākī*, 8. *Śavari svāhā*. At that time, within the assembly were the Heavenly Kings Vaiśravaṇa, Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Virūḍhaka, and Virūpākṣa, and others.
Each of them prostrated at the Buddha’s feet and addressed the Buddha,
saying: “World-Honored One, we four kings, relying upon the Buddha’s spiritual power,
also wish to bring benefit, peace, and happiness to all good sons and good daughters.”
I rejoice in the proclamation of this wondrous gateway of dharāṇī for prolonging life.
If there should be anyone who, at the time of early dawn,
gives rise to a heart of utmost sincerity and recites it according to the dharma, [they shall attain its benefits].
"We, the Four Kings, shall constantly provide protection,
ensuring there are no obstacles so that you may attain peace and security.
Then he spoke this dhāraṇī:

*Tadyathā:* (1) *puṣpe* (2) *supuṣpe* (3) *durmāparihāri* (4) *aryapraśaste* (5) *śānte* (6) *maṅgalaye nirmukte stute stute svāhā.* At that time, the World-Honored One extended his right arm of wondrous color.
He touched the crowns of the heads of Mahābrahmā, the Great Brahma King, and the Four World-Protecting Kings, and spoke these words: "Excellent, excellent!
You, Mahābrahmā, the Great Brahma King, and you World-Protectors."
For the sake of benefiting and bringing peace and happiness to all sentient beings,
and for the purpose of protecting and upholding the Buddha-dharma,
he has well expounded these subtle and wondrous phrases of the dhāraṇī.
Furthermore, the Buddha addressed the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi, saying:
"If there be sons or daughters of good family who give rise to a heart of utmost sincerity..."
Every morning at dawn,
one should recite according to the ritual procedure such dhāraṇīs as these, which are sublime gateways for prolonging life.
This person shall receive the empowerment and protection of all Tathāgatas,
as well as that of all the kings of devas, nāgas, yakṣas, asuras, garuḍas, gandharvas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, and vidyādharas.
"Even all humans and non-humans alike shall hold them in deep affection and respect;
they shall always be protected in every place and attain peace and security.
After the Buddha had spoken this sutra, [he entered parinirvāṇa].
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi and all the śrāvakas,
up to and including Mahābrahmā, the World-Protectors, and all devas, asuras, gandharvas, humans, non-humans, and so forth.
Having heard what the Buddha had spoken, they were all greatly rejoiced, and they believed, accepted, and practiced it accordingly.
The *Sūtra on the Dhāraṇī of the Sublime Door for Extending Life* Spoken by the Buddha.
